home-remodeling.title: Whole-House Remodeling in Davie, FL | PGX Builders
home-remodeling.meta_description: Acreage ranches and gated estate homes in Davie rebuilt end to end. Town of Davie permits, HVHZ glass, daily supervision. Call (786) 273-2524.
home-remodeling.hero_sub: Full-gut remodels for Davie acreage homes and gated-community estates alike: structure, mechanicals, impact openings and finishes, permitted through the Town of Davie Building Division and supervised on site every working day by a licensed general contractor.
intro_paragraphs: Davie is two housing markets wearing one town name. West of Flamingo Road you get acreage: 1960s through 1980s ranch houses on an acre or more along the Griffin Road and Orange Drive corridors, often with a barn, a paddock and a bridle trail at the property line. East and north sit the built-out gated communities: Long Lake Ranches, Imagination Farms, Forest Ridge, Grand Oaks Estates, where 1990s and 2000s estate homes have generous bones and dated everything. Whole-home remodeling here means solving one problem or the other.

The Town of Davie Building Division on Southwest 36th Street issues the permit, and it moved to online submittal through its OAS portal, so the plan set arrives as files rather than rolled paper. Above the town sits one more layer of authority: the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals, which maintains the county's amendments to the Florida Building Code, certifies the officials and inspectors who will review your job, and issues the formal code interpretations that settle arguments. Broward is High-Velocity Hurricane Zone territory too, so every new window, door and skylight needs current product approval.

PGX Builders Group has been building in South Florida for over 20 years, with 150-plus remodels and additions delivered and every one permitted and inspected. On a Davie whole-home job that shows up as a fixed written scope before the first wall comes down, a supervisor on site daily rather than a foreman who visits, and hard protection over the floors and stair rails you are keeping. Guard gates, contractor sign-in and quiet-hours rules in the gated communities are our problem, not yours. One team, one number to call, estimate through warranty.
home-remodeling.scope_heading: What a full Davie remodel covers
home-remodeling.scope_intro: Nothing starts until every line is written down and priced. On Davie houses, these five pieces do most of the heavy lifting.

scope_items.name: Walls down, beams up
scope_items.desc: Removing the load-bearing walls that chopped up 1980s ranch plans, with engineered beams, columns and footings sealed, permitted and inspected before the drywall returns.

scope_items.name: Service, panels and rewiring
scope_items.desc: New service, panels and branch wiring for houses built when two air handlers and a golf cart charger were nobody's plan.

scope_items.name: Impact openings, approvals attached
scope_items.desc: Windows and doors carrying valid Florida Product Approval or Miami-Dade NOA numbers, installed to the manufacturer's instructions because that is what the inspector checks.

scope_items.name: Roof and re-roof coordination
scope_items.desc: Sequencing tile or metal re-roofing with interior demolition so the house is never open to a July afternoon storm at the wrong moment.

scope_items.name: Well and septic realities
scope_items.desc: On acreage properties, checking what the existing septic system and well can support before the plan adds bathrooms, because the county health office will.

faqs.q: How long does the Town of Davie take to review remodel plans?
faqs.a: It depends on completeness far more than luck. Residential permits are filed as a master permit with the trades under it, and a clean, fully sealed package with product approvals attached tends to move in weeks rather than months. Missing structural calculations or a stale survey buys you a rejection cycle. We assemble the submittal so the first review is the one that counts, and we chase the corrections ourselves.

faqs.q: Who is the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals?
faqs.a: Indirectly, and constantly. BORA is Broward's code-administration layer: it maintains the county amendments to the Florida Building Code, certifies building officials, plans examiners and inspectors across every Broward municipality, recertifies the building departments themselves, and hears appeals and formal interpretation requests. You will never sit in front of it for a kitchen. But it is why a Broward plan review can differ from a Miami-Dade one on the same drawing, and why we submit differently on each side of the county line.

faqs.q: My community has an HOA architectural committee. Who approves what?
faqs.a: Both, in sequence, and the order matters. In Long Lake Ranches, Imagination Farms, Forest Ridge and the other guard-gated communities, the association reviews anything visible: roof color, window profiles, driveway material, exterior paint, generator and pool equipment placement. The Town of Davie reviews code and zoning. Association approval is not a building permit and a building permit is not association approval. We prepare both packages from the same drawings so the two do not contradict each other.

faqs.q: What is a realistic budget for a Davie remodel?
faqs.a: Honestly, the spread is enormous, because a cosmetic refresh inside a gated-community house and a full gut of an acreage ranch with new well equipment, added septic capacity and a new roof are different projects wearing the same label. What we commit to is a fixed written scope with named allowances, not a headline number that grows. PGX sits at the high end of the Broward market, and if low bid is the deciding factor we would rather say so at the first meeting.

faqs.q: Can we stay in the house while you remodel it?
faqs.a: On an acre lot with a guest house or a converted garage apartment, sometimes yes, and we phase the work to make that possible. In a full gut with the ceilings open, no air conditioning and one working hose bib, no. Davie families with horses on the property usually stay close and move into part of the house or a rental nearby. We will lay out the phasing honestly before demolition, including which weeks are genuinely unlivable.

home-remodeling.cta_sub: Bring the survey, the wish list, and the list of things that annoy you daily. You get straight answers and a written scope, in English o en español.

kitchen-remodeling.title: Custom Kitchen Remodels for Davie, FL Homes | PGX Builders
kitchen-remodeling.meta_description: Custom kitchen remodeling in Davie, FL: cabinetry, stone islands, layout changes and the electrical upgrades acreage homes need. Estimates at (786) 273-2524.
kitchen-remodeling.h1: The kitchen the ranch house never had
kitchen-remodeling.hero_sub: Custom cabinetry, stone counters and real layout changes for Davie kitchens, from Long Lake Ranches estates to acreage ranch houses. Permitted through the town, inspected, and run by a licensed general contractor, Lic. CGC1539072.
kitchen-remodeling.local_heading: Where the Davie kitchen goes wrong
intro_paragraphs: Davie kitchens fail in two predictable ways. The 1970s and 1980s ranch houses out on the Griffin Road acreage put a small galley behind a wall, facing the driveway instead of the pasture, with a pantry that used to be a closet. The 1990s and 2000s houses in Long Lake Ranches, Riverstone and Stonebrook Estates went the other direction: a vast room with a peninsula, a soffit at nine feet and forty linear feet of honey oak. Both get the same fix, from opposite directions.

A real kitchen remodel touches plumbing, electrical, mechanical and usually structure, which means a permit from the Town of Davie Building Division and inspections at each rough-in. There is no design board reviewing your cabinet doors; the town's Western Theme design manual governs the downtown district along Davie Road and Orange Drive, not your house. Two local wrinkles matter more. Acreage homes on well and septic need the county health office satisfied before the town will look at added fixtures. And if you enlarge a window over the sink, that new unit needs HVHZ product approval.

We build kitchens in an order that protects the money. Cabinets are ordered early and stored dry, stone is templated after boxes are set and never before, and the appliance specs are locked before rough-in so nobody is chiseling a gas line into finished tile. A fixed written scope, a supervisor here every working day, and floor protection from the front door to the job. Twenty-plus years in South Florida, more than 150 remodels and additions, all permitted and inspected. Your kitchen gets the same discipline.
kitchen-remodeling.scope_heading: What goes into a Davie kitchen
kitchen-remodeling.scope_intro: Cabinet drawings, stone slabs and appliance cut sheets get settled on paper first. Demolition is the last decision, not the first one.

scope_items.name: Cabinetry drawn for the room
scope_items.desc: Made-to-measure cabinet packages with finishes chosen to survive Broward humidity and a house that runs its air conditioning ten months a year.

scope_items.name: Islands and slab work
scope_items.desc: Slab quartzite, marble or granite measured off the installed boxes, with island framing sized for the weight and any seating overhang properly supported.

scope_items.name: Wall removal and beams
scope_items.desc: Opening the kitchen to the family room in block-and-tie-beam construction, with engineering, permits and inspections handled as part of the same package.

scope_items.name: Appliances moved, not squeezed
scope_items.desc: Relocating range, refrigeration and vent hood where the cooking actually happens, including new circuits, ducted exhaust to the exterior and gas or LP lines.

scope_items.name: Panel and lighting upgrades
scope_items.desc: Layered lighting on separate circuits, plus the service upgrade older acreage houses often need before an induction range and a wine column arrive.

faqs.q: Does a Davie kitchen remodel need a permit?
faqs.a: Yes, for anything past paint and pulls. Moving plumbing, adding circuits, re-ducting a hood or opening a wall all require a permit from the Town of Davie Building Division and inspections before things get covered. Since the town moved to online submittal, everything goes in as a sealed digital set. We file it, track the review comments and schedule the inspections, and you get the closed-out paperwork at the end, which matters at resale.

faqs.q: My house is on well water. Will that affect the kitchen?
faqs.a: It affects fixtures, filtration and the pot filler you have been picturing. Well water in western Davie often carries hardness and iron, which stains stone, clouds glass and shortens the life of cartridges in expensive faucets. We look at what treatment equipment is already on the property, size a filtration path for the kitchen, and specify finishes that tolerate the water you actually have rather than the water in the brochure.

faqs.q: Can I get a professional gas range if there is no gas line on my street?
faqs.a: Usually, with a propane tank. Plenty of Davie streets, particularly in the acreage sections, have no natural gas main, so a commercial-style range runs on LP from a tank set on the property. That means tank placement, setbacks, a permitted gas piping run and a pressure test, plus a supplier relationship. It is entirely doable and we do it regularly. It is also a reason to decide on the range before the cabinets are drawn.

faqs.q: How long will my kitchen be out of commission?
faqs.a: Cabinetry lead time sets the schedule, not demolition. Custom packages take months to build, so we order them first and keep your kitchen working until the boxes are close. Once we start, a straightforward kitchen typically runs a couple of months on site; add structural work, new gas piping or a floor replacement and it stretches. We set up a temporary kitchen with a sink and a refrigerator so the household still functions.

faqs.q: What does a high-end Davie kitchen cost?
faqs.a: Cabinetry and stone lead, appliances follow close behind, and the invisible work of electrical service, gas and structure decides whether the number surprises you. Rather than quote a per-foot figure, we measure, draw and price a specification you can hold. Expect a serious investment and a fixed written number tied to named products. We compete on execution and certainty, not on being the cheapest of three proposals.

kitchen-remodeling.cta_sub: Send us the floor plan or just open the door and point. A site visit, a real drawing, a fixed number, in English o en español.

bathroom-remodeling.title: Davie FL Bathroom Remodeling | PGX Builders Group
bathroom-remodeling.meta_description: Davie bathroom renovations built around septic loads and well water: tested pans, supported tubs, stone that holds up. Call (786) 273-2524.
bathroom-remodeling.hero_sub: Primary suites, guest baths and powder rooms across Davie: frameless glass, stone, freestanding tubs, and pans that get flood-tested before a tile is set. Permitted, inspected, and supervised daily by a licensed general contractor.
intro_paragraphs: The bathroom is the first thing that dates a Davie house and the last thing anyone budgets properly. Ranch homes in Shenandoah, Rolling Hills and out on the western acreage still carry the original hall bath with a steel tub, a 30-inch vanity and a window in the shower. The gated-community houses in Forest Ridge and Harmony Estates got a builder primary bath with a garden tub nobody has filled since 2004 and a shower built for one short person. Owners here consolidate: one genuine primary suite, and guest baths that stop apologizing.

Bathroom work in Davie is permitted through the Town of Davie Building Division, with plumbing, electrical and mechanical inspections along the way, and Broward's county amendments to the Florida Building Code apply as the Board of Rules and Appeals maintains them. The local complication is downstream. If your property is on septic, adding a bathroom or converting a half bath to a full one changes the load the system must carry, and the Florida Department of Health in Broward County, which still runs onsite sewage permitting locally, reviews that before the town issues anything. On sewer, you skip that step and go straight to plan review.

We treat a bathroom as a waterproof box that happens to have plumbing in it. The pan gets built, the membrane gets flooded and left overnight, and only then does tile arrive. Blocking for heavy glass goes in while the walls are open, niches are laid out to the tile module instead of to the plumber's convenience, and exhaust ducts to the outside rather than into an attic. Fixed written scope, daily supervision, licensed and insured under CGC1539072, permitted and inspected end to end.
bathroom-remodeling.scope_intro: Every fixture, tile size and drain location is settled on paper before the first sledgehammer. These are the pieces that come up most in Davie.

scope_items.name: Borrowing the spare bedroom
scope_items.desc: Absorbing an adjacent bedroom or oversized closet to build a real primary suite, with new plumbing runs, framing and permits handled as one package.

scope_items.name: Curbless and low-curb showers
scope_items.desc: Recessed pans where the slab allows, linear drains, and sloped substrates verified before waterproofing rather than discovered afterward by a puddle.

scope_items.name: Freestanding tubs, supported
scope_items.desc: Tub selection matched to floor structure and supply routing, with filler placement resolved before the slab goes down instead of after.

scope_items.name: Stone, tile and glass
scope_items.desc: Large-format porcelain, marble and quartzite set on flat substrate, with frameless enclosures templated to the finished walls so gaps stay honest.

scope_items.name: Septic-aware fixture counts
scope_items.desc: Checking existing drainfield capacity before the design adds a fifth bathroom, so the county health review is a formality instead of a redesign.

faqs.q: Will adding a bathroom overload my septic system?
faqs.a: It might, and that is a design question rather than a construction surprise. Onsite systems are approved for a certain load, and adding bathrooms or a full second-floor suite can push past it, which means expanding the drainfield or replacing the system. The county health office reviews and stamps that before the Town of Davie will issue a building permit. We investigate what is in the ground during the estimate, not during demolition.

faqs.q: Can I have a curbless shower on a concrete slab?
faqs.a: Often yes, sometimes with compromise. On slab-on-grade construction we cut and recess the pan area and reroute drain lines to get the slope without a curb, which is real work but routine. Where post-tension cables, shallow footings or an existing drain path make cutting a bad idea, a low-profile curb with a flush threshold gets you most of the look. We tell you which one your floor supports before the tile selection meeting.

faqs.q: Does well water damage bathroom finishes?
faqs.a: Untreated well water will mark polished nickel, etch nothing but stain everything, and leave orange shadows on white stone. In the acreage sections we check what softening or iron removal is already installed, size treatment where it is missing, and choose finishes and grout that hide the water chemistry you have. It is a cheaper conversation before the marble is ordered than after the first month of showers.

faqs.q: How long does a primary bathroom take?
faqs.a: Plan on a couple of months on site for a full primary bath, longer if we are moving walls or rebuilding the closet with it. The waiting is not glamorous: flood tests take a night, mortar beds and self-levelers need to cure, and slab glass is templated only after the tile is finished, then fabricated. Rushing any of those three is exactly how a bathroom fails. We schedule the cure times instead of pretending they do not exist.

faqs.q: What does a high-end bathroom remodel run?
faqs.a: Wide range, and the drivers are not where people expect. Stone and glass are visible costs; the ones that move a budget quietly are structural changes, drain relocation, septic implications and the electrical work behind heated floors, steam or a proper exhaust path. We scope the room after we see what is behind the walls, then give you one fixed written number. As a high-end contractor we sell certainty and finish quality rather than the lowest proposal.

bathroom-remodeling.cta_sub: Show us the room and tell us what you want it to feel like. We come back with a scope and a number, in English o en español.

home-additions.title: Davie, FL Home Additions & Guest Houses | PGX Builders
home-additions.meta_description: Guest houses, rear wings and second stories on Davie acreage lots. Permits, septic and engineering handled by a licensed GC. (786) 273-2524.
home-additions.h1: Build into the acre you own
home-additions.hero_sub: Rear extensions, second stories, garage conversions, guest suites and in-law quarters for Davie homes. Engineered, zoned correctly, permitted through the Town of Davie, and supervised on site by a licensed general contractor.
intro_paragraphs: Davie is one of the few places left in Broward where the lot is not the constraint. Rural Ranches and Agricultural parcels run an acre and up, and Estate Dwelling lots are generous by county standards, so the room you need usually fits behind the house you have. The projects follow the land: a primary wing added to a low-slung 1970s ranch off Griffin Road, a second story over a Grand Oaks Estates house whose footprint is maxed by setbacks, a detached guest house near the barn on a Flamingo Road acreage parcel for family who visit for a season.

Davie's rules stack up fastest on an addition. Zoning comes first: the RR, A-1 and R-1 districts each set their own lot coverage, setbacks and accessory-structure limits, and a guest house is a different animal from a bedroom wing. Then the Town of Davie Building Division reviews the structural set, with Broward's county code amendments and HVHZ product approvals applied at plan review. On septic and well properties the county health office weighs in on added fixtures. Much of the town sits in a special flood hazard area within the C-11 basin, so floodplain requirements and elevation certificates enter the conversation early.

Additions are the part of this business that punishes optimism, which is why we front-load them. Soil and structure get evaluated before drawings, the new foundation is designed to move with the old one rather than against it, and the roof tie-in is detailed so the seam disappears from the street. While the shell goes up, the occupied half of the house stays clean, conditioned and separated by hard barriers. One accountable team from feasibility through final inspection and warranty, and a scope you signed that does not quietly change.
home-additions.scope_heading: How Davie houses gain square footage
home-additions.scope_intro: Each of these starts with zoning and engineering, not with a rendering. We confirm what the parcel allows before anyone falls in love.

scope_items.name: Rear wings and extensions
scope_items.desc: Primary suites, family rooms and expanded living space pushed into the back yard, with footings, tie-beams and roof framing engineered and permitted together.

scope_items.name: Second stories over ranches
scope_items.desc: Structural evaluation of existing block walls and footings first, then a full upper floor with a stair that does not eat the plan below.

scope_items.name: Detached guest houses
scope_items.desc: Separate quarters where zoning permits them, with utilities, septic capacity and accessory-structure rules confirmed before the design gets ambitious.

scope_items.name: Garage and lanai conversions
scope_items.desc: Turning garages and screened lanais into conditioned rooms with insulation, HVHZ-rated openings and permitted mechanical work that survives an appraiser's questions.

scope_items.name: Foundations, steel and tie-beams
scope_items.desc: Underpinning, new footings, columns and tie-beam upgrades: the half of the budget nobody photographs and the half that decides whether it holds.

faqs.q: Can I build a guest house on my Davie acreage?
faqs.a: Frequently, and it is one of the most common requests we get out west. Whether a detached accessory dwelling is permitted, how big it can be, how far it must sit from property lines and whether it can have a full kitchen all depend on your zoning district and the parcel size. Utilities matter just as much: a second structure on well and septic is a capacity question before it is a design question. We check the zoning and the ground before drawing anything.

faqs.q: Does the flood map affect my addition?
faqs.a: It can, and in Davie it often does. A large share of the town falls inside a special flood hazard area, so an addition may need to meet floodplain construction requirements, and finished floor elevation gets documented with an elevation certificate. If the work is extensive enough to count as substantial improvement measured against the building's value, the whole structure can be pulled into compliance. That analysis belongs at the feasibility stage, before you commission architectural drawings.

faqs.q: How many months does an addition really take?
faqs.a: Think in seasons. Survey, design, structural engineering, zoning verification, health department review where septic is involved and then building permit review typically consume several months before a shovel moves. Construction of a substantial wing or second story runs several months more, with the shell and dry-in phase weather-dependent. A year from handshake to furniture is a fair expectation for a real addition. We publish the whole schedule in writing so nothing is a mystery.

faqs.q: Will an addition disturb my horses, barn or pasture access?
faqs.a: Not if it is planned properly, and this is a genuine Davie question. We map staging, material deliveries, concrete truck routes and dumpster placement to keep them away from paddocks, wash racks and the trail access at your property line. Crews get told where they may and may not walk. Heavy equipment days are scheduled with you in advance. The animals notice construction either way, but a tidy, predictable site is a lot easier on everyone.

faqs.q: What does an addition cost in Davie?
faqs.a: Per-square-foot numbers are the least useful figure in construction, because the same 600 square feet costs wildly different amounts depending on foundation, roof geometry, whether it is a second story, and whether the septic and electrical service can absorb it. We price additions after engineering and agency review are understood, and the result is a fixed written scope with named allowances. PGX builds at the high end. We are transparent about that at the first meeting rather than the last.

outdoor-living.title: Outdoor Living & Exteriors in Davie, FL | PGX Builders
outdoor-living.meta_description: Acreage backyards in Davie, FL get covered lanais, plumbed summer kitchens and driveways that hold up. Permitted and engineered. (786) 273-2524.
outdoor-living.h1: Outdoor rooms with an acre behind them
outdoor-living.hero_sub: Covered terraces, summer kitchens, pergolas, driveways, stucco and exterior work for Davie properties. Engineered footings, permitted utilities, HVHZ openings, and a licensed, insured general contractor running the site.
intro_paragraphs: Nobody moves to Davie for a patio. They move for space, and the back yard is where that pays off: an acre of St. Augustine, a pool, a paddock fence and a sunset with nothing between you and it. So outdoor projects here are built at a different scale. A covered lanai deep enough to sit under in a September downpour behind a Long Lake Estates house. A summer kitchen and shaded dining terrace at Imagination Farms. Paver driveways long enough to need drainage design, and a fence line that has to keep horses in and dogs out.

Exterior work is permitted through the Town of Davie Building Division like everything else, and roofed structures need engineering for uplift because Broward is High-Velocity Hurricane Zone territory. A pergola is not a weekend purchase; it is a permitted structure with footings, anchors and calculations. Summer kitchen gas, water and electrical get their own trade permits and inspections. New impervious paving raises drainage questions in a town where most land drains into the C-11 basin, and tree work can involve county environmental permitting. In the gated communities, association design approval comes before all of it.

The outdoor scope gets specified as carefully as any room indoors, which sounds obvious until you have seen a summer kitchen wired with an extension cord. Utilities are permitted and inspected. Footings are poured to an engineer's detail. Grades are set so water leaves the slab and heads for the swale instead of pooling against the house. Materials get chosen for sun, rain and fertilizer overspray rather than for a showroom photograph. Fixed written scope, a supervisor here daily, and a site that stays tidy because your neighbors did not sign up for this.
outdoor-living.scope_intro: Terraces, utilities, structures and paving get designed as one project so the drainage, the gas line and the roof line agree with each other.

scope_items.name: Covered lanais and terraces
scope_items.desc: Roofed outdoor rooms engineered for uplift, tied into the existing structure properly, with ceilings, fans and lighting finished to interior standards.

scope_items.name: Summer kitchens wired and plumbed
scope_items.desc: Permitted gas or LP, water, drainage and dedicated circuits, plus weather-rated cabinetry and stone that survives Broward sun instead of just surviving delivery.

scope_items.name: Pergolas and shade structures
scope_items.desc: Freestanding and attached structures with engineered footings and hurricane anchorage, sized to the house rather than to whatever the catalog offered.

scope_items.name: Driveways, aprons and paving
scope_items.desc: Long paver or finished-concrete drives on acreage lots, laid with base preparation and pitch so a rainy-season afternoon does not end at your front door.

scope_items.name: Stucco, paint and re-roof
scope_items.desc: Exterior restoration, color changes and re-roof coordination sequenced with the outdoor build so scaffolding and tile deliveries happen once, not three times.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a pergola or covered patio in Davie?
faqs.a: Yes. Anything with a roof or a permanent structure is a building permit, and in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone it needs engineered footings and connections designed for uplift, not lag bolts into a slab edge. The gas, water and electrical runs for an outdoor kitchen carry their own trade permits and inspections. If your community has an architectural committee, its approval comes first. We handle the whole sequence as part of the job.

faqs.q: Can I add a big paver driveway or motor court on my acreage lot?
faqs.a: Usually, with attention to drainage and coverage. Zoning districts set limits on how much of the parcel can be covered, and adding impervious paving changes where water goes on a property that likely drains toward the C-11 canal system. We design the pitch, the swales and any required retention so runoff stays on your land instead of your neighbor's, and we confirm setbacks and coverage before ordering a single pallet of pavers.

faqs.q: What holds up outdoors in this climate?
faqs.a: Not much, if it was chosen for the photo. Out here the enemies are UV, afternoon rain, irrigation with well water and lawn chemicals. We specify marine-grade or powder-coated stainless for outdoor kitchens, dense sealed stone or high-quality porcelain for surfaces, aluminum or properly treated structural members, and hardware rated for exposure. Cabinetry marketed as outdoor is not all equal. Spending correctly once beats replacing a grill island in five years.

faqs.q: Should I do the re-roof and impact doors at the same time as the terrace?
faqs.a: If both are on the list, yes, and the savings are real. Roof tie-ins for a new covered lanai are far cleaner when the roof is being replaced anyway, and swapping sliding doors to the back yard is easiest while that wall is already opened up and scaffolded. New openings need current HVHZ product approval regardless. Bundling means one permit strategy, one mobilization and one crew answering for the whole envelope.

faqs.q: What does a full backyard build cost out here?
faqs.a: Structure and utilities move the number far more than square footage does. A paver terrace is one conversation. A roofed outdoor room with a full summer kitchen, gas, water, drainage, lighting and a television that survives humidity is another entirely. Appliance and stone selections swing the number as much as size does. After a site walk we put a written specification and a fixed price in front of you, so you are comparing real scope rather than optimistic guesses.

permitting-compliance.local_heading: A town desk with rural rules
intro_paragraphs: Permit trouble in Davie is usually inherited, and it is usually big. A barn out on a Griffin Road acreage parcel grew an apartment for a working student. A lanai behind a Forest Ridge house was glassed in and quietly became a family room. A generator, a well pump house and a second panel arrived across three decades and two owners. The property shows beautifully. Then a buyer's title search or a lender's appraiser pulls the permit history on the address, and a project nobody planned starts on a deadline nobody chose.

Davie issues its own permits. The Town of Davie Building Division on Southwest 36th Street takes the Broward County Uniform Building Permit Application, and everything uploads through the town's OAS portal rather than crossing a counter. Status and inspection history stay attached to the folio, which is exactly where a title company looks. Davie also zones for horses and agriculture, so an acreage parcel raises setback, barn and accessory-structure questions a subdivision lot never sees. Broward sits above all of it through the Board of Rules and Appeals, and the whole county is High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, so glass, doors and roofing carry approved products.

Two decades of South Florida work and 150-plus remodels and additions, all of them permitted and inspected, teach you to price the record before you price the job. We list every permit the folio has ever carried, mark what was signed off and what stalled, and hand you that in writing. Where a barn, a guest suite or a well house has to be legalized, we retain the surveyor or engineer whose seal the town will actually accept. Septic capacity and flood elevation get checked early on an acre, because they decide what can be fixed on paper and what needs a machine. Lic. CGC1539072.
permitting-compliance.scope_heading: Files we open, files we close
permitting-compliance.scope_intro: Some of this starts as a drawing. Plenty of it starts as a letter from a title company. Both get the same first step: pull the record, then price the fix.

scope_items.name: Permits open on acreage
scope_items.desc: The town's permit record read line by line against what is actually standing on the lot, then revived, amended or re-inspected until the town closes the file for good.

scope_items.name: Work nobody ever filed
scope_items.desc: Glassed-in lanais, garage bedrooms, barn apartments and panels added off the books: surveyed as built, engineered where the structure needs it, then inspected against today's code.

scope_items.name: HVHZ openings on paper
scope_items.desc: Windows, doors, garage doors and roof assemblies matched to a current Florida Product Approval or Notice of Acceptance, and anchored the way that approval actually specifies.

scope_items.name: Inspections to a signed final
scope_items.desc: Each phase requested in an order the house can genuinely deliver, with a PGX supervisor on site to meet the inspector, so the last signature actually happens.

scope_items.name: Septic, well and elevation
scope_items.desc: Added fixtures cleared with the county health office, well equipment verified, and finished-floor elevation documented before a floodplain question parks your permit in review.

faqs.q: Our closing is coming up and there is an open permit on the house. What now?
faqs.a: Start with the file, not the wall. The address pulled up in the town's permit records shows every permit taken out, every inspection signed, and the point where somebody stopped calling. From there it is a diagnosis. The final may never have been requested. What stands may no longer match what was approved. The permit may belong to a contractor whose license lapsed years ago. Each has a path and none of them is fast, so make the call the day the title report lands, not the week of closing.

faqs.q: What actually needs a permit on a Davie property?
faqs.a: More than owners expect. Structure, roofing, windows and doors, electrical, plumbing, gas or LP, mechanical, pools, decks, fences, driveways and demolition all do, and adding fixtures on a septic property goes through the county health office first. Paint, flooring over a sound slab and a like-for-like swap generally do not. The Davie wrinkle is agricultural: state law exempts genuine nonresidential farm buildings on bona fide farm property, and that exemption is far narrower than owners assume. A barn with an apartment in it is not a farm building.

faqs.q: Does 40-year recertification or a milestone inspection apply to a Davie house?
faqs.a: Not to a house. Broward's building safety inspection program runs through the county Board of Rules and Appeals, keys off building age, and excludes one- and two-family dwellings: every house in Long Lake Ranches, Forest Ridge and the acreage. Florida's milestone inspection and structural integrity reserve study rules reach condominium and cooperative buildings of three habitable stories or more, a far shorter list here. Those reports are sealed by a licensed engineer or architect, not by us. We engage that professional, then permit and build the repairs it calls for.

faqs.q: We enclosed the lanai years ago without a permit. Do we have to tear it out?
faqs.a: Usually not. The normal path is an after-the-fact permit: an as-built survey and drawings, an engineer's evaluation of what is holding the roof up, selective demolition so an inspector can see framing, footings and wiring, then openings brought to current HVHZ approval and the electrical brought to code. Where it gets expensive is a room framed on a patio slab with no footing under it, or a bearing wall opened without a beam. Worth knowing: unpermitted square footage does not appraise, which is why lenders find it before buyers do.

faqs.q: What does it cost to legalize unpermitted work in Davie, and how long?
faqs.a: Both answers are behind the drywall. A permit missing only its final is a small line item. A guest suite framed over a patio slab with nothing engineered under it, or a roof laid with products that were never approved, can mean taking it apart and rebuilding to current code. Permit fees are set by the town and scale with the value of the work. Plan in weeks rather than days, start ahead of a closing date, and expect the number and the bad news in the same written scope.

permitting-compliance.cta_heading: Start with what the town has
permitting-compliance.cta_sub: Give us the address and whatever the town, the title company or a lender mailed you. You get a written path to a closed permit, in English o en español.
